gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS R3500 + SP039 600 W kit, which ships now, costs $0.554 per Wh through our link ($1,753.93 ÷ 3,168 Wh) and needs 5.3 hours of full sun at rated output to refill from its own panels (3,168 Wh ÷ 600 W). Every 3 kWh kit the rival pages list costs more per Wh: the cheapest, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra + 2×220 W, is $0.68/Wh and needs 7.0 hours at rated output.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited; 24 kits, $/Wh and refill hours, checked 2026-11-08), Eco Solar Kits (refill hours, Wh/lb and usable Wh for the HomePower 3000 kit only), Lights On Labs (cited; $/Wh and refill hours from 2026-10-27 prices) and EnergySage and SolarGenAdvisor (cited; SolarGenAdvisor would not load because of a certificate error). None of them lists an ALLPOWERS R3500 kit or any price paid through a code, and none gives a whole-kit weight. They already use the $/Wh and refill-hours measures, so the new part is the kits and the prices, not the measures themselves. Eco Solar Kits also says the Apex 300 has no built-in solar input, but Notebookcheck shows it does.
decides: The shipping rule requires a pick that ships now. Of the kits in range, the R3500 + SP039 600 W ships now and beats every rival-listed 3 kWh kit on both $/Wh and refill hours, so it is the pick among kits we link. The R3500 + SP037 400 W also ships now and is cheaper per Wh ($0.501), but it refills more slowly (7.9 h). For a shopper who can wait, the BLUETTI Elite 300 + 2×200 W ($0.535/Wh, pre-order, late November 2026) is the cheaper option. It only fits on battery size, because its AC output is 2,400 W. The Apex 300 kits are 3,840 W but cost $0.71–0.89/Wh and do not dispatch until late January 2027. Among rivals, the Jackery HomePower 3000 + 2×200 W, at $0.70/Wh and 7.7 h on StormWatts' Nov 8 figures, remains the best-known alternative.
